2689_2023.note: Same basis, no explanation of the restatement anywhere in either filing. The 2023 table is an internally consistent restatement of the paid and incurred history of the 2020 and 2021 years (both inflated by about 97m in total versus the 2022 table and the 2023 accounts' paid/incurred flows) that leaves outstanding unchanged. M = +42.378m is therefore a difference of cumulative figures that the accounts' own gross flows (58.2m incurred, of which at most about 7m for the 2021-and-prior years) cannot support; and the 104m measured from the 2022 report's diagonal is worse. The 2023 net table (p47) shows the same restatement (2021 net one year later 94,274 and two years later 136,650, i.e. +42.4m in 2023 against the net 9.26m stated on p7). Neither the 2022 nor the 2023 report states what caused it. Not a 2023 transaction: no 2023 RITC or transfer; the only RITC (2019 and prior to Syndicate 1254, immediately after 31 December 2021) is in the 2022 opening balance and does not touch the 2020-2022 years. Whether the 2022 table or the 2023 table is the faulty one is not decidable from the pages, but the 2023 table does not tie to the 2023 flows. The 2023 table's M is not a genuine 2023 development of the 2020-2021 years.
